premise: I poured my $102,000 widow’s inheritance into restoring a vintage 1920s carousel with my half‑brother, notarizing a 50/50 share and a promise of free rides for my grandkids; after a theme‑park chain offered $750,000 he forged a sale document, sold the carousel, and mailed me a $4,500 “fair share” check. I found our original agreement inside a hollow carved horse, voided the sale, and now run “Carousel of Lies” — he buffs brass poles in a vest that says “Rounding Up Fraud,” and every ticket prints his perjury docket.
